chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man performs one prayer completely, all of his prayers are accepted, even if they are not complete; and if he spoils all of them, nothing is accepted from him, nor is an optional prayer or an obligatory one reckoned for him; and indeed, the optional prayer is only accepted after the acceptance of the obligatory prayer; and when the man does not perform the obligatory prayer, the optional prayer is not accepted from him, and the optional prayer is made only to complete what was spoiled of the obligatory prayer.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the acceptance of optional prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the hierarchical dependency of supererogatory prayers (nafilah) on the validity of obligatory ones (fardh), a principle often cited to explain why neglected fardh prayers invalidate subsequent nafilah. It highlights the pedagogical purpose of nafilah as a means to rectify minor defects in obligatory acts, reinforcing the concept that spiritual merit is built upon a solid foundation of duty. This view aligns with the Shia emphasis on the integrity of the primary worship before engaging in voluntary enhancements.
